title: Why Leaves Change Color in Autumn
meta_description: Find out why chlorophyll fades in autumn, how yellow, orange and red pigments appear, and why weather and tree species create different fall colors.
h1: Why Leaves Change Color in Autumn?
author: Suraj Dahal
key_takeaways: Chlorophyll absorbs light for photosynthesis and makes healthy leaves look green; as days shorten and temperatures change, many deciduous trees stop replacing it and chlorophyll breaks down.
Carotenoids already present in leaves contribute yellow and orange tones that become visible as green pigment fades.
Some trees produce anthocyanins in autumn, contributing red and purple colors; sunlight, temperature, sugars and species influence how vivid those colors become.
Weather affects timing and intensity, but there is no universal calendar date for autumn color, and evergreen plants follow different strategies.
